info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package serve is the access decision behind an org-scoped call: who may do what, where, answered allow or deny.

post.summary: Ask whether a subject may act on an object
post.description:
Answers one policy question — may this subject take this action on this object — against the CALLER'S OWN org policy set, and answers it with a bare allow/deny.

The org comes from the gateway-minted X-Org-Id and picks the per-org enforcer, so a decision is always rendered by that tenant's policies and never by another's. A request carrying no org is refused rather than answered from a shared or default set: collapsing tenants together is the one failure a policy engine must not have.

Body: {sub, obj, act}, all three required. The reply echoes them beside `allow` so a cached or logged decision carries the question it answered.

get.description: Reports that the authz process is up. Unauthenticated by design and never org-scoped: it answers while every tenant's enforcer is still cold, because a probe that needed a tenant would fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the process being alive.

Reports that the authz process is ready to serve decisions. Unauthenticated and not org-scoped, for the same reason health is: readiness is a property of this process, not of any one tenant's policy set.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
